reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a compact topological measurable space with measurable open sets, and let mu:R->ProbabilityMeasure E be continuous in the standard weak topology. Let g:E->R be arbitrary, and let A:R x E->R be jointly continuous. Fix s in R. Define F(u)=Integral_E g d mu(u) and B(v)=Integral_E A(v,x) d mu(v)(x), using Lean's totalized real Bochner integrals. Suppose that for all u in some neighborhood of s, F(u)-F(s)=Integral_s^u B(v) dv. Then F has a two-sided derivative at s as a function on all R, and F'(s)=B(s). In particular no measurability or integrability hypothesis is imposed on g; without integrability, F(u) is the totalized value rather than an ordinary integrable expectation.
objects: Compact topological measurable state space E with measurable opens.
Arbitrary real function g, jointly continuous real function A(v,x), fixed real s.
Totalized expectation function F and drift expectation B.
domains: mu is defined and continuous on all R.
A has domain R x E; g has domain E.
HasDerivAt concerns the full real-domain function F at s, not a restricted-domain derivative.
quantifiers: For every admissible E,mu,g,A and every s satisfying the local balance assumption.
The balance identity is eventually true for u in nhds s: there is a neighborhood of s on which it holds for all u.
The conclusion is a pointwise derivative at this fixed s, not merely an AE assertion.
assumptions: E is compact and has measurable open sets; no metric, Hausdorff, second-countability or BorelSpace equality hypothesis is explicit.
A is continuous jointly in time and state.
No measurability, continuity, boundedness or integrability is assumed for g.
conclusion: The derivative value is Integral_E A(s,x) d mu(s)(x). Compactness and continuity ensure this particular integrand is bounded and integrable.
scopes: All occurrences of g are inside totalized Bochner integrals.
The balance hypothesis holds on a full real neighborhood of s and thus controls both sides of s.
No balance identity outside some neighborhood, no global differentiability and no specified modulus are asserted.
constant_dependencies: Compactness provides bounds on A over fixed compact time sets if needed; no uniform bound on all real times is a premise or conclusion.

semantic_checks.totalized_integrals: Critical: g is arbitrary and may be nonmeasurable or nonintegrable against mu(u). Lean defines the real Bochner integral to be zero when integrability fails, so the theorem differentiates the resulting totalized function. It must not be rewritten as an ordinary-expectation theorem with an unstated integrability premise. A(v,.) integrals are genuine by continuity and compactness.
semantic_checks.ae_pointwise_order: The assumption uses eventually in nhds s, not AE in Lebesgue measure. The derivative is pointwise at s.
semantic_checks.pushforwards: mu is an arbitrary given probability-law curve; no map from a process or pushforward representation is assumed.
semantic_checks.interval_orientation: Integral_s^u is oriented and the neighborhood includes u<s as well as u>s.
semantic_checks.compactness: Compactness of E is explicit; no compactness assumption on the full time domain.
semantic_checks.zero_endpoints: s is any real number, including zero or negative. u=s is included in the local balance and gives the zero increment.
semantic_checks.absolute_continuity: No explicit absolute-continuity premise or conclusion.
semantic_checks.derivative_domain: Full two-sided HasDerivAt on R at s, not HasDerivWithinAt on a half-line.
